chunks.content: # CLO x Blender Integration Workflow This document details the technical workflow for integrating CLO animations and costumes with Blender, focusing on animation recording, export settings, model importing, material setup, lighting, and final rendering. Key terms include FBX, Alembic (Ogawa format), UV rendering, node-based texturing, and HDR lighting. --- ## Animation Preparation and Export from CLO This section explains how to prepare and export animations and costumes from CLO for use in Blender, covering animation recording, UV rendering, export formats, and critical settings. - **Animation Recording**: Record the animation in CLO and verify playback before export. After recording, delete the animation layers because Blender cannot directly recognize multiple animation layers. - **UV Rendering**: Perform UV rendering within CLO by clicking the UV rendering icon to generate the necessary UV maps for texturing in Blender. - **Exporting the Model and Animation**: - Export the main model in **FBX format**. The FBX file path must not contain Chinese characters to avoid import issues in Blender. - When exporting, select the virtual model and choose a **single target**; multiple targets will prevent animation data from being included. - Choose **thick** for mesh thickness and select **unified UV coordinates**. - Enable options for **model action** and **save animation**. - Set the unit ratio correctly because Blender uses meters as the unit of measurement. - Confirm export with default settings unless specific adjustments are needed. - **Exporting Costume Animation**: - Export costumes using the **Alembic format**, specifically the **Ogawa format** variant. - Select the OCC format for costumes. - No special selection is needed for the location screen during export. - Default time sampling settings usually involve storing one data point every two time units (e.g., seconds), with sampling based on frame numbers rather than absolute time. --- ## Importing and Setting Up in Blender This section covers importing the exported CLO files into Blender, managing animations, and preparing the scene for texturing and rendering. - **Importing Files**: - Open Blender, press **A** to select all and delete default objects. - Import the model via **File > Import > FBX**. - Adjust animation start frames to zero to align timelines. - Import the costume via **File > Import > Alembic**. - **Scene Setup**: - Hide unnecessary objects such as the Google reference objects to clean the viewport. - Play the animation to verify correct import and check for any issues. - Hide all variables or unused layers to optimize scene management. - Expand the animation timeline and soften transitions if needed to smooth the animation playback. --- ## Material and Texture Application This section describes how to apply textures and materials to the imported CLO models and costumes in Blender using node-based shading and UV images. - chunks.title: CLO Tips Mini-Class - CLO x Blender Integration Workflow
chunks.content: --- ## Material and Texture Application This section describes how to apply textures and materials to the imported CLO models and costumes in Blender using node-based shading and UV images. - **Switch to Color Mode**: Change the viewport shading to color mode to preview textures clearly. - **Using Node Wrangler Add-on**: Enable and use the **Node Wrangler** plugin for efficient node management. - **Texture Setup Procedure**: 1. In the Shader Editor, create a new material. 2. Add a **Principled BSDF** shader node. 3. Press **Ctrl + Shift + T** to open the texture import dialog and select the UV image previously exported from CLO. 4. Connect the texture nodes accordingly to the Principled BSDF. 5. Adjust brightness and other parameters to fine-tune the material appearance. --- ## Scene Lighting and Camera Setup This section explains how to create lighting, set up the camera, and adjust the environment for realistic rendering in Blender. - **Adding Lighting**: - Add lights by selecting and clicking the light icon. - Use HDR images as an environment light source by switching to the **World** tab. - Add an **Environment Texture** node and load an HDR image to simulate realistic lighting. - **Camera Controls**: - Press **Shift + A** to add a camera. - Enter camera view by pressing the **Numpad 0** or by clicking the camera icon. - Adjust the camera position and angle by selecting the camera and using the viewport navigation controls or the **View > Cameras** menu. - **Rendering Mode**: Switch to the rendering preview mode to check lighting and material effects before final rendering. Note that the scene may appear black without a light source. --- ## Final Rendering Settings This section outlines the final steps to configure rendering attributes and produce the finished image or animation. - Configure render settings such as resolution, samples, output format, and frame range in Blender's **Render Properties** panel. - Perform the final rendering by clicking **Render > Render Image** or **Render Animation** depending on the project needs. - Review the output to ensure lighting, animation, and materials appear as expected. --- # Summary This workflow bridges CLO and Blender for 3D garment animation and rendering. Key steps include preparing and exporting animations and costumes from CLO in FBX and Alembic formats, importing and adjusting these assets in Blender, applying textures using node-based materials, setting up scene lighting with HDR environments, and finalizing renders with camera and render configuration. Following this structured process enables efficient and accurate integration between the two software platforms.
